rationale: Upstream directory layout is preserved deliberately. A uid is built from the file path, so include/fmt/os.h and src/os.cc are distinct modules — flattening the fixture put them in one directory and manufactured 14 header/source uid collisions that do not exist in the real repository. Keep the subdirectories. C++ has a genuinely low ceiling and this floor is deliberately not near 1.0. tree-sitter has no preprocessor, so every unexpandable macro is a token the grammar must guess at, and fmt is macro-dense (FMT_BEGIN_NAMESPACE, FMT_CONSTEXPR, FMT_API, gtest's TEST). Almost every uncaptured named function is stranded behind a compound_statement or ERROR in its ancestor chain — the enclosing namespace or class failed to parse and collapsed into a bare block, so the function survives but its scope does not. Emitting entities for them was rejected: the name is recoverable but the qualified name is not, and a Callable with a wrong qn resolves to the wrong target rather than to nothing. Their calls are still recovered, because _extract_calls descends into that debris and attributes to the nearest scope that did survive (ADR-0031). The full 72-file checkout scores named_funcs 0.690 / calls 0.937 / duplicate_uids 492, so this fixture tracks it closely on all three. The 7.6% call shortfall is dominated by C++ named casts (static_cast/reinterpret_cast/const_cast/dynamic_cast), which the grammar shapes exactly like calls but which are keywords, not callables — an edge to one could never resolve; the rest is calls with no static callee name at all (fp[i](), (*fp)(), chained f()()). ROUTING: .h is shared between C and C++ and is now routed by sniffing the content (sniff_header_is_cpp), not by the extension alone. This replaced the earlier note here that the routing bug was unfixed — it is fixed. Measured against 583 real C headers from CPython 3.14, Python 3.13 and site-packages, the sniff flips 13, and every one of those genuinely contains C++ inside an #ifdef __cplusplus block (pyatomic_std.h's `extern "C++"`, mimalloc's STL allocator, dynamic_annotations.h's `template <class T>`, PyWin32's COM headers): zero flips on a header that is C-only. Against fmt's 25 headers it flips 23; the two it leaves are correct — fmt-c.h is fmt's actual C API header, and core.h contains nothing but #includes. Comments and string literals are blanked before matching, because in CPython every mention of `class` or `namespace` outside those dual-language headers is prose; and each marker demands syntactic context, because C reserves none of these words and CPython really does ship a `namespaceSeparator` field. DUPLICATE UIDS ROSE, 11 to 49, and that is the routing fix working rather than a regression to hide: parsing headers as C++ made 100 more Callables visible in this fixture (212 to 312), and C++ overloading means more entities on one name. 45 of the 49 are same-file overloads and constructors — scan.h alone contributes 9 basic_scan_arg constructors and 8 read overloads — which need the signature in the uid, a cross-cutting schema change. The other 4 are a different and newly reachable shape worth naming: a class member declared in test/gtest-extra.h and defined out-of-line in test/gtest-extra.cc collides, because a header and its implementation sitting in the same directory under the same stem produce the same module qualified name. Merging them is arguably right — they are one function — but the winner is arbitrary, so the surviving node may carry the declaration's empty body instead of the definition's source. That shape is not new to this change (a .hpp/.cpp pair beside each other always did it); routing simply made .h/.cc pairs reach it too.
